key_insight: A unified statistical framework combines passage-level signals to audit whether individual documents or collections were used to train an LLM.
clinical_relevance: For medical AI, this approach could support audits of training-data provenance and potential benchmark contamination involving medical question-answer records.
method: Combine complementary chunk-level membership evidence using Cauchy combination to score documents.
Use calibrated document-level p-values to assess training use across a target collection.
Apply multiple testing to identify suspicious documents with false discovery rate control.
evidence_signal: Case studies on BookTection, Pile-arXiv, Cosmopedia, and HealthCareMagic evaluated audits of pre-training and fine-tuning data; the abstract reports effectiveness and reliability without numerical results.
watch_item: Statistical guarantees depend on stated exchangeability conditions, which require scrutiny before applying the framework to new medical datasets.
paper_title: A Statistical Framework for Training Data Auditing of Large Language Models
